summary: Real security fix not yet on main. Removes raw token URLs (resetUrl, inviteUrl) from email_events DB metadata in email-service.ts. PR #1311 was closed without merging; the specific email-service.ts fix was never re-implemented in any subsequent merged PR.

commits.detail: Removes resetUrl from sendPasswordResetEmail metadata and inviteUrl from sendPilotInviteEmail metadata — both contained raw tokens that should never be stored in DB

commits.message: test: E2E test verifying token URLs not stored in email_events metadata
commits.detail: 153-line E2E test verifying that email_events metadata does not include raw token URLs

evidence.confirmationOfMiss: git grep on origin/main shows email-service.ts still has `resetUrl: data.resetUrl` (line ~521) and `inviteUrl: data.inviteUrl` (line ~802) passed to sendEmail() metadata — the raw token URLs are still being stored in email_events table

evidence.siblingNote: Siblings address different aspects (admin token timing-safe comparison, blast route, static analysis guards) — none re-implement the email-service.ts metadata fix

securityAssessment.issue: Raw password reset URLs and pilot invite URLs are logged to email_events.metadata in PostgreSQL. These URLs contain full plaintext tokens. A DB read compromise exposes all active reset links and invite links.
securityAssessment.fixCorrectness: The orphan branch fix is minimal and correct — removes the URL fields from metadata while retaining agentName and other non-sensitive fields. The actual email still sends the full URL to the user.

recommendation: Create a new PR from this branch (or cherry-pick both commits) onto main. The fix is small (6 lines in email-service.ts), correct, and addresses a real security gap that survived multiple rounds of token-related fixes. Do NOT delete this branch until the fix is re-landed.
